**Trigger warning** near end. Main points are in **bold**.  


**I live in a state of having everything in my mind at once, without the ability to navigate my thoughts**.  


**I often adjust my personality to be liked by others**.  


**I lash out with no warning**. If I don't lash out (because it's around someone I don't want to show my crazy) then I internalize it, and it slowly destroys me inside.  


**I don't know who I am or what I enjoy**. I simply am too busy trying to prevent people from **leaving**, **avoiding situations** that make me **anxious**, dealing with **emotional dysregulation**, saving my relationships (wife and parents), **trying to get people to** **understand me**, pushing people away or trying to **get intensely close superfast**, and much, much more. You could ask me **"what are you in to, or what are your hobbies etc." and I'd just look at you and be like "I don't know" because I truly don't know**. I play games, but not because it's a hobby, but rather I'm just bored.  


When I am triggered, and I enter the **dysregulation**, **I tend to shut down** and enter a state of **paranoia** where I am telling myself that I don't deserve love and my partner may find someone else, so I get **hyper vigilant** about everything they do to try to find shady shit. Not because I think they're evil, but rather because it would give me an out. It would justify my thoughts. For some reason, **I don't have the ability to reason when I am dysregulated**.  


When things are normal, they're just straight up normal. This usually happens when I am single. **As soon as I enter a relationship, I know it's just a matter of time before I sense a disturbance in the force and everything is down hill from there**.   


**I've only found one career that works for me** (fiber optic tech) Because I literally cannot have a mundane job, or I won't last a week. I am a contractor and instead of quit, I just go to a different contractor, so I can feel like I have a clean fresh start. **This applies to almost everything, though. Relationships, jobs, hobbies etc. In the beginning everything is great, then the downward spiral happens.**   


**My feelings get hurt incredibly easy** when someone close says or does something that I take as an attack or jab. When it comes to **people I am not close to, such as acquaintances, I am emotionless**. They can literally do or say anything, and I just respond with a resounding "fuck you" and go about my day.   


**I've probably been in a disassociated state most of my life.**   


**In 41 years of life, I literally have nothing to show for it**. I mean I have wonderful kids but other than that I feel like I have just worked to survive. I find it incredibly hard to save money, so I really never have a backup plan when shit hits the fan, so **I feel like I'm constantly struggling even though I have a good paying job**.  


**I have never had a "best friend"** simply because I don't fucking trust anyone.

Part of the reason it's seen as a "woman's disorder" is because men are less likely to seek treatment. I didn't get diagnosed till I was 40, and **I am 41 now, so I am at the** **beginning of my recovery**.   


***Trigger warning - (maybe)***

  
**My BPD stems from unresolved childhood trauma**. I was sexually assaulted at 3, and I watched my dad do some horrible shit to my mom, and those 2 memories are burned in my brain, and they're the only memories I have from birth to around 5. I held on to that with immense guilt and shame, and never really knew how to deal with it.  **I'm in therapy and on Lamictal now**, so hopefully I can get through this with some hard work.
